quiz.title: Quiz 3 - Exercise 2C
quiz.source_reference: M1, Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line, Exercise 2C, Questions 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16. Questions: Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf. Worked solutions: Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf (Exercise C). © Pearson Education Ltd 2008.
quiz.instructions: Model each object as a particle and neglect air resistance. Use g = 9.8 m/s² and round final numerical answers to 2 significant figures. Where a question has several parts, choose the option with every part correct. Keep full precision until the final answer.

questions.title: 2C Q1
questions.prompt: A ball is projected vertically upwards from O at \(14\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find its greatest height above O.
questions.working:
Take upwards as positive, so \(a=-9.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). At the highest point \(v=0\).

From \(v^2=u^2+2as\), \(0=14^2-19.6s\).

\[s=\frac{196}{19.6}=10\,\mathrm{m}.\]
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2C, Question 1; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 23; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 37 (Exercise C, Question 1).

questions.title: 2C Q2
questions.prompt: A well is \(50\,\mathrm{m}\) deep. A stone is released from rest at the top. Find the time it takes to reach the bottom.
questions.working:
Take downwards as positive, with \(u=0\), \(a=9.8\) and \(s=50\).

\[50=\frac12(9.8)t^2=4.9t^2.\]

The positive root is \(t=\sqrt{50/4.9}=3.19438\ldots\), so \(t=3.2\,\mathrm{s}\) (2 s.f.).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2C, Question 2; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 23; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 38 (Exercise C, Question 2).

questions.title: 2C Q4
questions.prompt: A particle is projected vertically upwards from the ground at \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find its time of flight until it returns to the ground.
questions.working:
Take upwards as positive. At the return to the ground, \(s=0\):

\[0=20t-4.9t^2=t(20-4.9t).\]

Reject \(t=0\), the launch instant. The flight time is \(20/4.9=4.08163\ldots\approx4.1\,\mathrm{s}\) (2 s.f.), not just the time to the highest point.
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2C, Question 4; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 23; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 40 (Exercise C, Question 4).

questions.title: 2C Q6
questions.prompt: A pebble is catapulted vertically upwards at \(24\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find (a) its greatest height above the point of projection and (b) the time taken to reach that height.
questions.working:
Take upwards as positive; at the highest point \(v=0\).

(a) \(0=24^2-19.6h\), giving \(h=29.3878\ldots\approx29\,\mathrm{m}\) (2 s.f.).

(b) \(0=24-9.8t\), so \(t=24/9.8=2.44898\ldots\approx2.4\,\mathrm{s}\) (2 s.f.).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2C, Question 6; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 23; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 42 (Exercise C, Question 6).

questions.title: 2C Q8
questions.prompt: P is projected vertically downwards from \(80\,\mathrm{m}\) above the ground at \(4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find (a) its speed on impact and (b) its time to reach the ground.
questions.working:
Take downwards as positive: \(u=4\), \(a=9.8\), \(s=80\).

(a) \(v^2=4^2+2(9.8)(80)=1584\), so \(v=\sqrt{1584}=39.7995\ldots\approx40\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) (2 s.f.).

(b) Use the unrounded impact speed:

\[t=\frac{\sqrt{1584}-4}{9.8}.\]

Thus \(t=3.65301\ldots\approx3.7\,\mathrm{s}\) (2 s.f.).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2C, Question 8; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 23; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 44 (Exercise C, Question 8).

questions.title: 2C Q10
questions.prompt: A ball is thrown vertically upwards at \(21\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and hits the ground \(4.5\,\mathrm{s}\) later. Find the height above the ground from which it was thrown.
questions.working:
Take upwards as positive. After \(4.5\,\mathrm{s}\),

\[s=21(4.5)-4.9(4.5)^2=-4.725\,\mathrm{m}.\]

The ground is below the launch point. The requested height is the positive magnitude \(4.725\approx4.7\,\mathrm{m}\) (2 s.f.), not the signed displacement.
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2C, Question 10; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 23; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 46 (Exercise C, Question 10).

questions.title: 2C Q11
questions.prompt: A stone is thrown vertically upwards at \(16\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) from \(3\,\mathrm{m}\) above the ground. Find (a) its time of flight and (b) the total distance it travels before hitting the ground.
questions.working:
Take upwards as positive. The final displacement from launch is \(-3\,\mathrm{m}\).

(a) \(-3=16t-4.9t^2\), so \(4.9t^2-16t-3=0\).

\[t=\frac{16+\sqrt{314.8}}{9.8}.\]

The negative root is not an elapsed flight time. The positive root gives \(t\approx3.4\,\mathrm{s}\) (2 s.f.).

(b) The rise above launch is \(h=\frac{16^2}{19.6}=13.0612\ldots\,\mathrm{m}\). The descent is \(h+3\).

Total distance \(=2h+3=29.1224\ldots\approx29\,\mathrm{m}\) (2 s.f.). Keep full precision until the final rounding.
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2C, Question 11; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 23; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 47 (Exercise C, Question 11).

questions.title: 2C Q12
questions.prompt: A particle is projected vertically upwards at \(24.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the total time for which it is \(21\,\mathrm{m}\) or more above its point of projection.
questions.working:
Take upwards as positive. The two crossings of height \(21\,\mathrm{m}\) satisfy \(21=24.5t-4.9t^2\).

\[4.9t^2-24.5t+21=0.\]

The quadratic formula uses denominator \(2(4.9)=9.8\):

\[t=\frac{24.5\pm\sqrt{188.65}}{9.8}.\]

The crossing times are \(1.09847\ldots\) and \(3.90153\ldots\,\mathrm{s}\). Between them the height is at least \(21\,\mathrm{m}\).

Their difference is \(2.80306\ldots\approx2.8\,\mathrm{s}\) (2 s.f.).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2C, Question 12; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 23; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 48 (Exercise C, Question 12).

questions.title: 2C Q15
questions.prompt: A ball is released from rest \(10\,\mathrm{m}\) above a wooden floor. Each impact is followed by a rebound at three-quarters of the impact speed. Find its greatest height above the floor after (a) the first rebound and (b) the second rebound.
questions.working:
The first impact speed is \(\sqrt{2(9.8)(10)}=14\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

(a) The first rebound speed is \(\frac34(14)=10.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

\[h_1=\frac{10.5^2}{19.6}=5.625\,\mathrm{m}.\]

Thus \(h_1\approx5.6\,\mathrm{m}\) (2 s.f.).

(b) The second impact speed is again \(10.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), and the second rebound speed is \(\frac34(10.5)=7.875\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

\[h_2=\frac{7.875^2}{19.6}=3.1640625\,\mathrm{m}.\]

So \(h_2\approx3.2\,\mathrm{m}\) (2 s.f.). The height ratio per rebound is \((\frac34)^2\), not \(\frac34\).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2C, Question 15; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 24; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF pages 51–52 (Exercise C, Question 15).

questions.title: 2C Q16
questions.prompt: P is projected vertically upwards from O at \(12\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). One second later Q is projected vertically upwards from O at \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find (a) the time from P's launch until they collide and (b) the height of the collision above O.
questions.working:
Take upwards as positive and let \(t\) be the time since P's launch. Q has been in flight for \(t-1\) seconds.

\[s_P=12t-4.9t^2.\]

\[s_Q=20(t-1)-4.9(t-1)^2.\]

(a) Equating displacements gives \(24.9=17.8t\), hence \(t=\frac{24.9}{17.8}=1.39888\ldots\approx1.4\,\mathrm{s}\) (2 s.f.). This is measured from P's launch, not Q's.

(b) Substitute the unrounded time into \(s_P=12t-4.9t^2\). This gives \(s_P\approx7.2\,\mathrm{m}\) (2 s.f.).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2C, Question 16; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 24; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 53 (Exercise C, Question 16).
